Works even on variable-depth trees — every leaf item gets its own NEW deepest branch level regardless of starting depth (e.g. a 4-branch variable-depth tree becomes 8 branches, each N=1). Also available as a right-click menu option on any parameter/input.

Canonical worked case [STATED] ("4 triangles -> 12 vertices"): a 4-branch x 3-item vertex tree is Flattened to {1x12}, then Unflattened using the ORIGINAL pre-flatten tree as guide, restoring the exact 4x3 structure. Split Tree.name: Split Tree
Split Tree.behavior: Mask-string grammar: `{;;}` enclose the branch-selection mask, `[]` enclose the element/leaf-selection mask (omitted = select all, `[*]`); `()` for grouping. Wildcards: `*` matches any number of integers in a path; `?` matches any single integer; a bare integer matches that value; `!` negates a rule; comma-list `(2,6,7)` matches any listed value (negatable); range `(2 to 20)` matches an inclusive range (negatable); open arithmetic sequence `(0,2,...)` matches integers in that ascending sequence, optionally bounded `(0,2,...,48)` — a negated infinite sequence `!(3,5,...)` does NOT extend leftward, so it also matches everything below the sequence start; rules combine with and/or, e.g. `{*}[(0 to 4) or (6,11,41)]`. BOTH outputs retain the EXACT original tree structure (same branch paths/item counts) — excluded elements are replaced with null, not removed — enabling lossless recombination via Combine Data after independently transforming one side. Also demonstrated splitting by whole alternating BRANCH indices (mask at the branch level, e.g. `{0,2,...}`) rather than within-branch elements, for "treat whole columns differently" cases.

Needed in addition to (not instead of) Graft when repeated Explode/Graft chains accumulate over-nested branches, before Merge+Loft will pair curves correctly. Related but separately-named cleanup tools mentioned only in body text: Clean Tree and Trim Tree (remove null elements/empty branches), Explode Tree (splits all branches into separate list outputs). CORRECTED: the KB's prior guess of "mask or 'L' for levels" for the second input was wrong — it is "Front" (F), a boolean.

Internally builds two NEW correlated trees (A tree, B tree) whose corresponding branches/items are exactly the described pairs, so a simple 2-point Line A→B draws all offset connections at once. Necessarily produces OUTPUT trees SMALLER than the input whenever the offset references an out-of-bounds branch/index (e.g. the last branch/item has no +1 neighbor) — both outputs trim to only addresses where both base and offset target exist.

Path Mapper.behavior: "Perhaps the least intuitive to use and can cause a loss of data," but "the only way to find a solution in some cases." Three named constants for expressions: item_count (items in current branch), path_count (branches in whole tree), path_index (index of current branch). Typical expressions use tuple notation `{A;B;C}` for a 3-level path and `(i)`/`[i]` for item index, e.g. regroup `{A;B;C}->{A;C;B}`, or flip (promote item index into path, demote a path level into item index) `{A;B;C}[i]->{A;B;i}[C]`; composable into one expression, e.g. `{A;B;C}[i]->{A;C;i}[B]` (saves processing vs. chaining two Path Mappers — "not always possible"). Right-click presets: Mapping Editor, Create Null Mapping (no-op template), Create Flatten Mapping, Create Graft Mapping, Create Trim Mapping, Create Reverse Mapping (reverses item order per branch, structure unchanged), Create Renumber Mapping (strips nested path structure to flat sequential top-level branch numbers), Enabled, Help.

Branch.name: Branch

inputs.name: P
inputs.description: Path, as text or Path parameter

Branch.behavior: Extracts a single branch from a tree given its explicit path address (e.g. "{0;0;0}"); can also be fed a dynamically-derived path (e.g. from Tree Statistics + List Item, using -1 wrap-around indexing for "last branch") instead of hardcoding.
Branch.provenance: [STATED, Essential p.65] (has a "Maintain" mode label per source)

Tree Statistics.name: Tree Statistics

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: Paths — list of all branch path addresses

outputs.name: L
outputs.description: branch element counts, one number per branch

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: branch Count, total number of branches

Tree Statistics.behavior: Used to dynamically extract path addresses (e.g. for feeding Branch) instead of typing them, and to reconstruct a point list from an XYZ-organized tree.

Concatenate.name: Concatenate
Concatenate.tab: Sets > Text (RESOLVED — AAD wins; Essential's "near Maths" grouping is a thematic/teaching grouping, not the component's actual ribbon tab)
Concatenate.behavior: Joins text fragments into one string; used for literal sentences and for assembling parametric condition expressions (e.g. a slider value concatenated after "x>").

Cull Duplicates.name: Cull Duplicates
Cull Duplicates.behavior: Mode option "Average" used to detect coincident/duplicate points (e.g. face centroids of touching mesh-box faces) within tolerance — a -1 index entry marks a point with no duplicate (genuine boundary), paired index entries mark coincident/overlapping points to be culled. Used in a "cull adjacent/internal faces" cleanup strategy for joined mesh-box aggregations.

Series.name: Series
Series.behavior: Generates an arithmetic numeric sequence; default S=0,N=1,C=10 → (0..9); negative N gives a decreasing sequence. Setting Start=0 makes the first generated element coincide with the un-translated original object.

Random.name: Random
Random.behavior: Generates N random real numbers within domain R; deterministic given a fixed seed — same seed always reproduces the same list. Right-click "Integer Numbers" switches output to integers.

Range.name: Range

outputs.name: R
outputs.description: list of N+1 numbers spanning domain D

Range.behavior: Divides a numeric domain into N equal parts, returning N+1 values inclusive of both ends — contrast Series, which is not domain-bound. GOTCHA: to get exactly one value per existing object, subtract 1 from the object count (via Subtraction) before feeding Range's N-input, or lists are off-by-one.

Unit X.name: Unit X
Unit X.behavior: Default unit vector along the world X-axis, scalable via F (embedded scalar multiplication).

Unit Z.name: Unit Z
Unit Z.behavior: Default unit vector along world Z-axis, magnitude 1 unless scaled via F; used pervasively for gravity/self-weight loads and "move up by height" translations.

Vector XYZ.name: Vector XYZ

outputs.name: L
outputs.description: "Length", Number — magnitude of the constructed vector

Vector XYZ.behavior: Alternative to Unit X/Y/Z shortcuts — builds a vector from three explicit numeric components.

Vector 2Pt.name: Vector 2Pt
Vector 2Pt.behavior: A single boundary edge can supply both plane-origin points (via Divide Distance) and a single constant slicing direction (via Vector 2Pt) for a family of parallel cutting planes.

Vector Length.name: Vector Length
Vector Length.behavior: One of two equivalent ways to get a curvature value (the other: 1/osculating-circle-radius via Deconstruct Arc + Division).

Amplitude.name: Amplitude
Amplitude.behavior: Rescales a vector to a target length while preserving direction/sense. In the surface-conforming Weaving tutorial, driven by the LOCAL surface normal (from Divide Surface) rather than a fixed world direction, so a woven pattern can conform to any surface — explicit warning: "make sure the data structure of normals and points match."

Distance.name: Distance
Distance.behavior: Computes the distance between two points; used to measure attractor-to-geometry distance, and (with a target value) as the Fitness basis for goal-seeking optimization.

Construct Point.name: Construct Point
Construct Point.behavior: Computes a point from x/y/z; distinct from the container "Point" component despite sharing the "Pt" abbreviation on canvas. Default input data 0,0,0 places a point at the world origin.

Deconstruct (point) / Point Decompose.name: Deconstruct (point) / Point Decompose
Deconstruct (point) / Point Decompose.behavior: Used as a sort-key source (feed X or Y output into Sort List's K) to recover grid order from geometry when list order is scrambled.

DePlane.name: DePlane
DePlane.behavior: Deconstructs a plane into origin + 3 axis vectors; used as an intermediate step to extract a circle's plane/origin so Scale can use it as the scale center.

outputs.name: Pl
outputs.description: a new plane with B's orientation relocated to origin O

Plane Normal.name: Plane Normal
Plane Normal.behavior: Builds a plane from an origin + a normal vector (e.g. a surface normal from Evaluate Surface), used to derive a rotation plane from geometry, or a panel's local offset direction for non-coplanar panel arrays.

Construct Plane.name: Construct Plane

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: "X-Axis", Vector — X-axis direction of the plane

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: "Y-Axis", Vector — Y-axis direction of the plane

Construct Plane.behavior: CORRECTED — a real, distinct component from Plane Normal (above), not a probable duplicate. It builds a plane from an origin plus explicit X- and Y-axis vectors (3 inputs), not from an origin plus a single Z/normal vector as previously guessed by analogy. If AAD p.269's partly-illegible diagram genuinely showed only two inputs (O and one vector), that diagram was more likely depicting Plane Normal (or another 2-input plane constructor) rather than this 3-input component.

Square Grid.name: Square Grid

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: Points, tree — one branch per row/column

Square Grid.behavior: Ex controls the number of tree branches in the output point tree; Ey controls the number of items per branch.

Reverse (vector).name: Reverse (vector)

outputs.name: V
outputs.description: "Vector", Vector — reversed vector, i.e. multiplied by -1

Reverse (vector).behavior: Used to invert a face-normal direction when it does not match the required sense relative to another vector (e.g. a solar-ray vector) — direction requirement is context-dependent (e.g. must point inward for one recipe, outward for another); always verify with Vector Display first. CORRECTED/MERGED: this is the same real component as the KB's separate "Negate (vector)" entry (AAD p.376, gravity-vector usage feeding Catenary's G input) — both describe a Vector > Vector sign-flip with identical V→V ports. No standalone "Negate" component exists in GH1; the two AAD citations (p.376 and p.451/454) are merged into this one entry.
Reverse (vector).provenance: [STATED, AAD p.451, 454] [STATED, AAD p.376 as "Negate"/alias "Neg" — merged, same component] [VERIFIED https://grasshopperdocs.com/components/grasshoppervector/reverse.html]

Circle (plane + radius).name: Circle (plane + radius)
Circle (plane + radius).behavior: Constructs a circle from a plane and radius — the first Grasshopper component shown in AAD, wired to a Radius slider.

Circle CNR (center + normal + radius).name: Circle CNR (center + normal + radius)
Circle CNR (center + normal + radius).behavior: Builds the circle's plane implicitly from a point+normal instead of a full Plane — convenient when normals come from curve/surface evaluation (e.g. Eval.T or Evaluate Surface.N). AAD explicitly names "Circle CNR"; Essential shows the identical port shape (center, normal, radius) simply labeled "Circle" — treated as the same component.
Circle CNR (center + normal + radius).provenance: [STATED, AAD p.112 (used unnamed as "Circle"), 178 (formally named), 204; Essential p.32, 46]

Arc 3Pt.name: Arc 3Pt

inputs.name: B
inputs.description: "Point B", Point — point the arc passes through

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: "Plane", Plane — the plane containing the arc

Arc 3Pt.behavior: Creates an arc through three points; A and C are endpoints, B is a point the arc passes through. Used to build a pre-set arc-length (e.g. forcing a 10-unit-span arc to have arc-length exactly 20) as the starting geometry for a near-inextensible catenary approximation.

Line (2-point).name: Line (2-point)
Line (2-point).behavior: Builds a line from two points; shows orange/warning if A/B unconnected, red/error if a wrong type is wired (e.g. a raw Number into a Point input — "Data conversion failed from Number to Point"). With two point lists (e.g. from dividing concentric circles), connects corresponding points; combining with Shift List on one list changes which points pair up, producing different radial/spoke patterns.

Line SDL.name: Line SDL
Line SDL.behavior: Builds a line from a start point + direction + length — distinct from the two-point Line component (A/B inputs); used e.g. to offset an "apex" point above a sub-surface center along its normal.

Point on Curve.name: Point on Curve

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: implicit) + value 0-1 (rendered as a slider-bar on the component's face

Point on Curve.behavior: Finds a point via fractional ARC LENGTH (not domain parameter t) — 0.5 is always the true geometric midpoint; does not require reparameterization. Right-click named snaps: 0.0(start)/1/4(quarter)/1/3(third)/1/2(mid)/2/3(two thirds)/3/4(three quarters)/1.0(end). CONTRASTS with Evaluate Curve (domain-parameter-based, not arc-length-based) — a Grasshopper-native substitute for CAD Osnap "midpoint" picking.

End Points.name: End Points
End Points.tab: Curve > Analysis (RESOLVED — AAD p.160's "Endpoint"/Curve > Util reference is an internal inconsistency, likely mislabeling of an in-context screenshot; "End Points"/Curve > Analysis is correct)
End Points.behavior: Extracts a curve's two endpoints — a Grasshopper-native substitute for CAD Osnap "endpoint" picking.
End Points.provenance: [STATED, AAD p.62, 160, 303, 366; Essential p.19 general list mention] [VERIFIED https://grasshopperdocs.com/components/grasshoppercurve/endPoints.html]

Evaluate Curve [DISAMBIGUATION 2 of 3 \u.name: Evaluate Curve [DISAMBIGUATION 2 of 3 — see Evaluate F(X) under Maths, Evaluate Length below]

outputs.name: A
outputs.description: "Angle", Number — angle in radians between the incoming vs. outgoing curve direction at t; a discontinuity measure, not curvature

Evaluate Curve [DISAMBIGUATION 2 of 3 \u.behavior: Finds point + tangent vector at DOMAIN parameter t — NOT arc-length (t=0.5 is generally NOT the true midpoint unless the curve is reparameterized AND happens to be uniform). Renders as a plain "Eval" box identical to Evaluate F(X) and Evaluate Length; distinguish by its C/t ports and Curve > Analysis tab. Combined with Random + Sort: Random generates unordered curve parameters, which MUST be Sorted (ascending) before feeding to Eval, else resulting points/circles are visited out of curve order, producing a twisted/self-intersecting Loft.

Evaluate Length [DISAMBIGUATION 3 of 3 \.name: Evaluate Length [DISAMBIGUATION 3 of 3 — see Evaluate F(X) under Maths, Evaluate Curve above]

inputs.name: N
inputs.description: "Normalized", Boolean — if True, L is read as a normalized 0.0-1.0 fraction of total curve length; if False, L is read as an absolute length in curve/model units; AAD's example implicitly uses N=False/absolute-length mode

Evaluate Length [DISAMBIGUATION 3 of 3 \.behavior: Finds the point located a given arc-length distance L from the curve's start (t=0). Renders as a plain "Eval" box identical to Evaluate F(X) and Evaluate Curve; distinguish by its C/L/N ports and Curve > Analysis tab.

Divide Curve.name: Divide Curve

inputs.name: K
inputs.description: "Kinks", Boolean — when True, adds extra split points at the curve's discontinuities/direction changes

outputs.name: T
outputs.description: "Tangents", Vector — tangent direction at each point

outputs.name: t
outputs.description: "Parameters", Number — the curve parameter at each point

Divide Curve.behavior: Divides an open or closed curve into equal arc-length segments: N+1 points for an open curve, exactly N points for a closed curve (e.g. dividing a circle into 5 gives 5 points, since start/end coincide). Output points ordered by the curve's parametric start-to-end direction. Dividing a SINGLE curve gives a flat list; dividing a LIST of curves gives a tree (one branch per curve) — a key example of components that add tree nesting.

Divide Length.name: Divide Length
Divide Length.behavior: Divides a curve into fixed absolute-length segments; leaves a "leftover-arc" of different length at the end if the curve's total length isn't an exact multiple of L.

Divide Distance.name: Divide Distance
Divide Distance.behavior: Divides a curve via sequential intersections of circles of radius D (centered at each successively-found point) with the curve — geometrically distinct from Divide Length. Leaves a leftover-arc if D doesn't evenly divide the curve. A single boundary edge can supply both plane-origin points (via Divide Distance) and a constant slicing direction (via Vector 2Pt) for parallel cutting planes.

Contour.name: Contour

inputs.name: D
inputs.description: Distance, Number — spacing between cutting planes

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: "Contours", Point — intersection points, grouped by section

outputs.name: t
outputs.description: "Parameters", Number — curve parameter of each contour point

Contour.behavior: Intersects a curve with a family of parallel cutting lines/planes spaced D apart along direction N, starting from point P.

Shatter.name: Shatter

inputs.name: t
inputs.description: list of split parameters, LCS [0,1] domain

Shatter.behavior: Splits a curve into segments AT given t-parameters — returns curve pieces, not points (unlike other Division-family components). The t-input can be a slider, Curve CP's t-output, or Divide Curve's t-output. RESOLVED: this is a real, distinct component from Explode Curve (Curve > Util, below). AAD p.378's diagram labeled "Explode" with ports C,R → S,V is NOT a mislabeled Shatter — its ports exactly match the real, separate Explode component's spec (Shatter has no R input and no V output), so it is the book's own surrounding text (still calling it "Shatter" in context on that page) that is wrong, not the diagram label.

Curvature.name: Curvature
Curvature.behavior: Returns the curvature vector and osculating circle (best-fit circle) at a point on a curve; k = |K| = 1/r (osculating circle radius).

Curvature Graph.name: Curvature Graph
Curvature Graph.behavior: Visually displays curvature along a curve as a comb of perpendicular hairlines, length proportional to curvature magnitude, +/- signs marking curvature-sign regions.

Flip Curve [shares nickname \"Flip\" wit.name: Flip Curve [shares nickname "Flip" with the unrelated Flip Matrix (Sets > Tree) — see that entry's disambiguation note]
Flip Curve [shares nickname \"Flip\" wit.behavior: Reverses a curve's parametric direction (swaps t=0/t=1 ends). With G supplied plus a list of mixed-direction curves at C, flips only curves not already matching G's direction, in one operation. Does NOT fix curve direction via Reparameterize — these are independent operations (direction is set by original control-point order).

Curve Closest Point.name: Curve Closest Point
Curve Closest Point.behavior: World-to-Local conversion for curves — finds closest point on curve to a given point, returns the distance; if P lies exactly on the curve, P=P' and D=0. Implements curve-based attractors.

Deconstruct Arc.name: Deconstruct Arc
Deconstruct Arc.behavior: Breaks an arc (incl. a circle, a closed arc) into base plane, radius, and angle domain.

Interpolate Curve (official GH1 name: \".name: Interpolate Curve (official GH1 name: "Interpolate")
Interpolate Curve (official GH1 name: \".behavior: Draws a curve interpolated through a list of points. Used repeatedly to fit a smooth curve through Kangaroo particle positions for visual continuity — a caveat applies: this can look smooth but is physically incorrect at multi-anchor junctions since it implies bending stiffness a hinge-particle simulation cannot have. CORRECTED (naming): the current GH1 component's official name is "Interpolate" (nickname "IntCrv"), not "Interpolate Curve" — a naming nuance, not a factual error in the port data. COMPLETED: the extra L/D outputs are real (Length, Domain), not an over-guess — the source's own hedge undersold what AAD/Essential correctly showed as 3 outputs.

Nurbs Curve.name: Nurbs Curve
Nurbs Curve.behavior: Rebuilds a smooth freeform curve through a point list — used to fix sharp-corner discontinuities introduced by a raw Offset, and to rebuild a smooth silhouette from a twisted-loft isocurve extraction. Confirmed to share the same L/D output pattern as Interpolate Curve, exactly as previously guessed by analogy.

Polyline.name: Polyline
Polyline.behavior: Operates PER BRANCH on tree-structured input — a component fed N branches produces N separate polylines, not one continuous one (core illustration of "branches are watertight").

Isocurve.name: Isocurve
Isocurve.behavior: Extracts the two isocurves passing through a given uv point.

Curve on Surface.name: Curve on Surface

inputs.name: uv
inputs.description: "UV coordinates", Point — list/tree of uv interpolation points, from Merge

inputs.name: C
inputs.description: "Closed", Boolean — whether the resulting curve is closed

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: "Curve", Curve — resulting NURBS curve coincident to the surface

Curve on Surface.behavior: Creates an interpolated curve on a surface through an arbitrary set of uv points in the surface's Local Coordinate System — used to build a Galapagos-optimized shortest path across a freeform surface. Note the component reuses nickname "C" for both an input (Closed) and an output (Curve).

Offset (curve).name: Offset (curve)
Offset (curve).behavior: Generic planar/3D curve offset (not surface-constrained — contrast Offset on Srf below). Offsetting a curve with sharp corners can introduce discontinuities/kinks at those corners — fix: divide the offset into many points and rebuild via Nurbs Curve.

Offset on Srf.name: Offset on Srf

inputs.name: S
inputs.description: surface(s) to keep the offset coincident to

Offset on Srf.behavior: Unlike a generic curve offset, keeps the result coincident with a host surface — required so an inward-offset "frame" curve of a curved panel stays flush with the panel sub-surface rather than drifting off it in 3D.

Explode Curve [3-WAY NAME CONFLICT: \"Ex.name: Explode Curve [3-WAY NAME CONFLICT: "Explode" is shared by this component (Curve > Util), by a Mesh > Util component that explodes a mesh into faces, and by a Mesh > Analysis "Mesh Explode" — disambiguate by tab and by whether the input is a curve or a mesh]
Explode Curve [3-WAY NAME CONFLICT: \"Ex.behavior: Breaks a polyline/polycurve into its constituent segments and vertices.

Discontinuity.name: Discontinuity
Discontinuity.behavior: Returns one branch of points per input curve (e.g. turns each Voronoi cell — a single closed curve — into its own branch of boundary vertex points).

Project.name: Project
Project.behavior: Projects a curve onto a target surface, replacing straight segments with true surface-coincident curves — essential post-step for diagrid construction (a diagrid floats off a curved surface except at corners; Project snaps it back).

Extrude.name: Extrude
Extrude.behavior: Extrudes a base curve/brep along a direction vector — "the easiest way to create a surface."

Loft.name: Loft
Loft.behavior: Generates a surface through a set of section curves.

Loft Options.name: Loft Options
Loft Options.behavior: Sets loft behavior; rebuild needed when too few section curves exist for a smooth surface.

Boundary Surfaces.name: Boundary Surfaces
Boundary Surfaces.behavior: Creates a flat planar surface bounded by closed curve(s); also usable as an implicit planarity test (only produces a surface if the boundary curves are planar).

Surface from Points.name: Surface from Points

inputs.name: P
inputs.description: Points — grid of points, must be pre-ordered row-by-row/column-by-column and set to flatten mode

inputs.name: U
inputs.description: U Count — number of points in u-direction, integer

inputs.name: I
inputs.description: Interpolate — boolean, interpolate a surface through the points vs. use them as control points

Surface from Points.behavior: Builds a surface from a rectangular grid of points; needs an explicit U count to know how many points lie in one direction (obtained e.g. via List Length on a Range output). WARNING: assumes the input list is already sequenced in row/column grid order — a geometrically-correct but list-order-scrambled point set produces a severely malformed, self-intersecting surface with NO error raised.

Edge Surface.name: Edge Surface
Edge Surface.behavior: Creates a surface interpolating between 2-4 ordered boundary/edge curves. Can only cap boundaries of exactly 4 edges — N-sided openings (e.g. hexagons) require a different capping strategy (two Lofts between opposite edge pairs, or Patch as a general alternative).

Patch.name: Patch
Patch.behavior: Fits a surface using perpendicular "span" curves generated from the input; spans rarely align with the output surface's edges — a fallback when other surfacing methods aren't feasible (e.g. general-purpose N-sided capping).

Network Surface.name: Network Surface

outputs.name: S
outputs.description: surface fit through the two curve families

Network Surface.behavior: Builds one surface from two ordered curve sets — more edge control than Loft. Also usable as an alternative weave finish: if warp/weft threads are allowed to touch (skip the Negative-vector step), the resulting curve network can be fed directly into Network Surface for one continuous quilted surface instead of discrete piped tubes.

Revolution.name: Revolution
Revolution.behavior: Revolves a profile curve around a fixed axis.

Rail Revolution.name: Rail Revolution

inputs.name: A
inputs.description: revolution axis line, per one usage

Rail Revolution.behavior: Revolves a profile using a rail curve instead of a fixed axis, letting the axis itself vary along the rail — used to rebuild a smooth-edged surface of revolution replacing a sharp-edged twisted Loft.

Pipe.name: Pipe
Pipe.behavior: Sweeps a circular cross-section of given radius along one or more rail curves — e.g. turns a wireframe diagrid into a tubular 3D structure, or a woven thread curve into a solid member.

Surface CP.name: Surface CP
Surface CP.behavior: World-to-Local conversion for surfaces (surface analog of Curve CP); if the input point lies on the surface, P=P' and D=0.

Divide Surface.name: Divide Surface
Divide Surface.behavior: Generates a grid of points at isocurve intersections dividing u/v evenly by the given integer counts. Dividing a single surface produces a TREE of points (a grid), one branch per row/column. Its natural U+1-branches x V-items output tree is exploited directly as the "warp" direction of a weave, and Flip-Matrix-transposed to get the "weft" direction for free.

Isotrim.name: Isotrim
Isotrim.behavior: Splits a surface into contiguous untrimmed sub-surfaces per a supplied grid of sub-domains (typically from Divide Domain²). Output sub-surfaces KEEP the original parent surface's domain (not reset to [0,1]) unless explicitly Reparameterized.

Deconstruct Brep.name: Deconstruct Brep
Deconstruct Brep.behavior: Extracts all constituent faces, edges, vertices of any Brep. When fed a list of N sub-surfaces at once, each downstream List Item(i=k) extracts "vertex slot k of every sub-surface" as one flat parallel list (implicit grouping, not explicit tree manipulation) — key to scaling single-item recipes (e.g. a diagrid) to whole-surface recipes.

Center Box.name: Center Box
Center Box.behavior: Builds a box primitive; output is a Brep not a single Surface — wiring directly into a Surface-typed parameter causes a red type-mismatch error; fix: Deconstruct Brep first.

Bounding Box.name: Bounding Box

outputs.name: B
outputs.description: second box output — e.g. axis-aligned vs. plane-aligned

Bounding Box.behavior: Right-click mode toggle: "Per Object" (one bbox per input geometry) vs. "Union Box" (one box enclosing all input geometries together).

Geodesic.name: Geodesic
Geodesic.behavior: Constructs the shortest-path curve ("straight line in curved space") between two points on a surface — used as a natural cutting curve for Surface Split, and (per a guest project) as the basis of a gridshell panelization pattern.

Surface Split.name: Surface Split
Surface Split.tab: Intersect > Physical (RESOLVED — see full entry under Surface tab above; cross-referenced here per its confirmed Intersect tab)
Surface Split.provenance: [STATED, AAD p.155, 178-179] [VERIFIED https://grasshopperdocs.com/components/grasshopperintersect/surfaceSplit.html] (see Surface tab for full entry)

Area.name: Area
Area.tab: Surface > Analysis (per book's own label, applied even to a planar closed curve)
Area.behavior: Computes area and centroid; used in attractor recipes purely for the centroid output ("center of each circle").

Principal Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nick.name: Principal Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nicknamed "Curvature" on canvas — same nickname as Surface Curvature below, disambiguate by outputs]

inputs.name: uv
inputs.description: point in UV domain, e.g. MD Slider

Principal Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nick.behavior: At point P on a surface, C1 = curve of minimum curvature K1, C2 = curve of maximum curvature K2 through P; directions always perpendicular.

Surface Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nickna.name: Surface Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nicknamed "Curvature" — see Principal Curvature above]
Surface Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nickna.behavior: G = K1·K2 (product of principal curvatures; G=0 developable, G>0 synclastic/dome, G<0 anticlastic/saddle); M = (K1+K2)/2 (M=0 defines minimal surfaces, e.g. catenoids/soap films). Signed-curvature convention: circles are defined as negative curvature, so e.g. a cylinder's M comes out negative — must Absolute-value before using as a physical quantity like radius.

Osculating Circles.name: Osculating Circles

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: Point — surface point at that uv

outputs.name: C1
outputs.description: First circle, Curve — first principal osculating circle

outputs.name: C2
outputs.description: Second circle, Curve — second principal osculating circle

Osculating Circles.behavior: Developability test: if the surface is developable at P, at least one of C1/C2 degenerates to a straight line (very-large-radius circle); test by piping into a Line-cast component — cast succeeds (valid) = line-like = developable there; cast fails (red/error) = genuine arc = not developable there via that direction. CORRECTED/MERGED: this is the same component previously also listed under "Tab unconfirmed" as "Oscillator" (AAD p.309, identical S,uv → P,C1,C2 shape) — "Oscillator" is not a real Grasshopper component name; that entry was a mistranscription/mislabeling of this one and is merged in here.
Osculating Circles.provenance: [STATED, AAD p.175-176] [STATED, AAD p.309 as "Oscillator" — merged, same component] [VERIFIED https://grasshopperdocs.com/components/grasshoppersurface/osculatingCircles.html]

Mesh Triangle.name: Mesh Triangle
Mesh Triangle.behavior: Builds one triangular mesh face by topology (index references into a separate vertex list, not raw points); winding order (CCW) determines front/back orientation. "Creating meshes by topology" strategy — suited to small point counts or repeating logics.

Construct Mesh.name: Construct Mesh
Construct Mesh.behavior: Assembles a mesh from a vertex list + face-index list (+ optional colors).

Delaunay Mesh.name: Delaunay Mesh
Delaunay Mesh.behavior: Triangulates an arbitrary point set maximizing minimum angle (avoids skinny/thin triangles that produce inaccurate FEM/particle-spring simulation results); formal rule: for each triangulated face, its circumscribed "Delaunay circle" must not contain any other point of the set. Operates per-branch on grafted/tree-structured input (one discrete disconnected mesh per branch — requires join+weld afterward to fuse).

Mesh Surface / Mesh UV.name: Mesh Surface / Mesh UV
Mesh Surface / Mesh UV.tab: Mesh > Util (RESOLVED — AAD p.450/456's "Mesh > Triangulation" citation is an internal inconsistency; Util is correct. Mesh > Triangulation is a real, separate panel too, home to Delaunay Mesh/Voronoi/TriRemesh — AAD appears to have conflated the two panels for this entry)

inputs.name: H
inputs.description: Overhang — allow faces to overhang trims, boolean

Mesh Surface / Mesh UV.behavior: NURBS-to-mesh conversion — reliable only for UNTRIMMED surfaces (clean rectangular isogrid maps directly to quad grid); trimmed surfaces only approximate their boundary via this component (Mesh Brep preserves exact boundary but risks skinny triangles near it). Best suited for large variable counts where no exact solver applies. Cannot be driven by a Graph Mapper (its internal curve is not slider-drivable, so it cannot itself be a Genome input — expose the sliders that feed it instead). Runs indefinitely; must be manually stopped once the top candidate's fitness stabilizes. Worked example: cantilever cross-section shape optimization (Karamba) — topology fixed, only CroSecSelect's index varies — reduced tip displacement from 0.009703 (index 29) to 0.000253 (index 89 optimum), ~38x improvement. Also used to find the shortest interpolated path between two fixed points on a freeform surface via Gene Pool-driven uv control points, and (per a guest essay) to re-solve a fabrication-constrained panelization for a smaller laser-cutter bed without redesigning the geometry.

87e1d9ef-088b-4d30-9dda-8a7448a17329.behavior: The most extreme possible un-flattening — turns a flat list into a tree with one branch per item. "Unintuitive" (complicates structure) but essential for full cross-product matching: grafting two independent lists (each item → own branch) before Merging causes per-branch components (e.g. Loft) to process matched pairs instead of one giant flattened concatenation. Works even on variable-depth trees — every leaf item gets its own NEW deepest branch level regardless of starting depth (e.g. a 4-branch variable-depth tree becomes 8 branches, each N=1). Also available as a right-click menu option on any parameter/input.

Canonical worked case [STATED] ("4 triangles -> 12 vertices"): a 4-branch x 3-item vertex tree is Flattened to {1x12}, then Unflattened using the ORIGINAL pre-flatten tree as guide, restoring the exact 4x3 structure. 41aa4112-9c9b-42f4-847e-503b9d90e4c7.name: Flip Matrix

outputs.name: D

41aa4112-9c9b-42f4-847e-503b9d90e4c7.behavior: Transposes an M-branch x N-item tree into an N-branch x M-item tree (matrix transpose) — used to regroup "corresponding" items (e.g. same point-index across several curves/threads) that started out grouped by source object. Requires uniform branch depth: variable-LENGTH branches get padded with literal `<null>` values to remain rectangular; variable-DEPTH branches (nested at different levels) make Flip fail entirely — component turns red/errors, "there is no logical solution to flip." NOTE: shares the on-canvas nickname "Flip" with the unrelated Flip Curve component (Curve > Util) — disambiguate by pins (Flip Matrix: D in/out; Flip Curve: C in/out) and tab.

d8b1e7ac-cd31-4748-b262-e07e53068afc.name: Split Tree
d8b1e7ac-cd31-4748-b262-e07e53068afc.behavior: Mask-string grammar: `{;;}` enclose the branch-selection mask, `[]` enclose the element/leaf-selection mask (omitted = select all, `[*]`); `()` for grouping. Wildcards: `*` matches any number of integers in a path; `?` matches any single integer; a bare integer matches that value; `!` negates a rule; comma-list `(2,6,7)` matches any listed value (negatable); range `(2 to 20)` matches an inclusive range (negatable); open arithmetic sequence `(0,2,...)` matches integers in that ascending sequence, optionally bounded `(0,2,...,48)` — a negated infinite sequence `!(3,5,...)` does NOT extend leftward, so it also matches everything below the sequence start; rules combine with and/or, e.g. `{*}[(0 to 4) or (6,11,41)]`. BOTH outputs retain the EXACT original tree structure (same branch paths/item counts) — excluded elements are replaced with null, not removed — enabling lossless recombination via Combine Data after independently transforming one side. Also demonstrated splitting by whole alternating BRANCH indices (mask at the branch level, e.g. `{0,2,...}`) rather than within-branch elements, for "treat whole columns differently" cases.

1303da7b-e339-4e65-a051-82c4dce8224d.behavior: Removes redundant/overlapping nested branch levels (e.g. `{0;0;0;0;0;0}` → `{0}`) without changing item counts or values. Needed in addition to (not instead of) Graft when repeated Explode/Graft chains accumulate over-nested branches, before Merge+Loft will pair curves correctly. Related but separately-named cleanup tools mentioned only in body text: Clean Tree and Trim Tree (remove null elements/empty branches), Explode Tree (splits all branches into separate list outputs). fac0d5be-e3ff-4bbb-9742-ec9a54900d41.behavior: Offset-string grammar "{branch offset}[index offset]" describes how to connect an item at one address to another item at a relative address in the SAME or a DIFFERENT tree — e.g. `{+1}[+1]` connects branch B/index I to branch B+1/index I+1 (diagonal grid connectivity). Internally builds two NEW correlated trees (A tree, B tree) whose corresponding branches/items are exactly the described pairs, so a simple 2-point Line A→B draws all offset connections at once. Necessarily produces OUTPUT trees SMALLER than the input whenever the offset references an out-of-bounds branch/index (e.g. the last branch/item has no +1 neighbor) — both outputs trim to only addresses where both base and offset target exist.

f9b89a46-bc5d-4f7a-9a6f-134f93ac3af9.behavior: "Perhaps the least intuitive to use and can cause a loss of data," but "the only way to find a solution in some cases." Three named constants for expressions: item_count (items in current branch), path_count (branches in whole tree), path_index (index of current branch). Typical expressions use tuple notation `{A;B;C}` for a 3-level path and `(i)`/`[i]` for item index, e.g. regroup `{A;B;C}->{A;C;B}`, or flip (promote item index into path, demote a path level into item index) `{A;B;C}[i]->{A;B;i}[C]`; composable into one expression, e.g. `{A;B;C}[i]->{A;C;i}[B]` (saves processing vs. chaining two Path Mappers — "not always possible"). Right-click presets: Mapping Editor, Create Null Mapping (no-op template), Create Flatten Mapping, Create Graft Mapping, Create Trim Mapping, Create Reverse Mapping (reverses item order per branch, structure unchanged), Create Renumber Mapping (strips nested path structure to flat sequential top-level branch numbers), Enabled, Help.

d63304ae-c240-5255-97d1-64a222fd4cdb.name: Branch

inputs.name: P
inputs.description: Path, as text or Path parameter

d63304ae-c240-5255-97d1-64a222fd4cdb.behavior: Extracts a single branch from a tree given its explicit path address (e.g. "{0;0;0}"); can also be fed a dynamically-derived path (e.g. from Tree Statistics + List Item, using -1 wrap-around indexing for "last branch") instead of hardcoding.
d63304ae-c240-5255-97d1-64a222fd4cdb.provenance: [STATED, Essential p.65] (has a "Maintain" mode label per source)

99bee19d-588c-41a0-b9b9-1d00fb03ea1a.name: Tree Statistics

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: Paths — list of all branch path addresses

outputs.name: L
outputs.description: branch element counts, one number per branch

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: branch Count, total number of branches

99bee19d-588c-41a0-b9b9-1d00fb03ea1a.behavior: Used to dynamically extract path addresses (e.g. for feeding Branch) instead of typing them, and to reconstruct a point list from an XYZ-organized tree.

2013e425-8713-42e2-a661-b57e78840337.name: Concatenate
2013e425-8713-42e2-a661-b57e78840337.tab: Sets > Text (RESOLVED — AAD wins; Essential's "near Maths" grouping is a thematic/teaching grouping, not the component's actual ribbon tab)
2013e425-8713-42e2-a661-b57e78840337.behavior: Joins text fragments into one string; used for literal sentences and for assembling parametric condition expressions (e.g. a slider value concatenated after "x>").

d9c2276d-1e11-5200-8469-301cbeaf1bc9.name: Cull Duplicates
d9c2276d-1e11-5200-8469-301cbeaf1bc9.behavior: Mode option "Average" used to detect coincident/duplicate points (e.g. face centroids of touching mesh-box faces) within tolerance — a -1 index entry marks a point with no duplicate (genuine boundary), paired index entries mark coincident/overlapping points to be culled. Used in a "cull adjacent/internal faces" cleanup strategy for joined mesh-box aggregations.

e64c5fb1-845c-4ab1-8911-5f338516ba67.name: Series
e64c5fb1-845c-4ab1-8911-5f338516ba67.behavior: Generates an arithmetic numeric sequence; default S=0,N=1,C=10 → (0..9); negative N gives a decreasing sequence. Setting Start=0 makes the first generated element coincide with the un-translated original object.

2ab17f9a-d852-4405-80e1-938c5e57e78d.name: Random
2ab17f9a-d852-4405-80e1-938c5e57e78d.behavior: Generates N random real numbers within domain R; deterministic given a fixed seed — same seed always reproduces the same list. Right-click "Integer Numbers" switches output to integers.

9445ca40-cc73-4861-a455-146308676855.name: Range

outputs.name: R
outputs.description: list of N+1 numbers spanning domain D

9445ca40-cc73-4861-a455-146308676855.behavior: Divides a numeric domain into N equal parts, returning N+1 values inclusive of both ends — contrast Series, which is not domain-bound. GOTCHA: to get exactly one value per existing object, subtract 1 from the object count (via Subtraction) before feeding Range's N-input, or lists are off-by-one.

79f9fbb3-8f1d-4d9a-88a9-f7961b1012cd.name: Unit X
79f9fbb3-8f1d-4d9a-88a9-f7961b1012cd.behavior: Default unit vector along the world X-axis, scalable via F (embedded scalar multiplication).

9103c240-a6a9-4223-9b42-dbd19bf38e2b.name: Unit Z
9103c240-a6a9-4223-9b42-dbd19bf38e2b.behavior: Default unit vector along world Z-axis, magnitude 1 unless scaled via F; used pervasively for gravity/self-weight loads and "move up by height" translations.

c844928a-0acf-59bf-89b7-e8dd9eb41e06.name: Vector XYZ

outputs.name: L
outputs.description: "Length", Number — magnitude of the constructed vector

c844928a-0acf-59bf-89b7-e8dd9eb41e06.behavior: Alternative to Unit X/Y/Z shortcuts — builds a vector from three explicit numeric components.

69a6e32c-51b6-53e9-8c70-744de2fdf928.name: Vector 2Pt
69a6e32c-51b6-53e9-8c70-744de2fdf928.behavior: A single boundary edge can supply both plane-origin points (via Divide Distance) and a single constant slicing direction (via Vector 2Pt) for a family of parallel cutting planes.

8204e027-2b1d-5a71-8ec5-11a868ae6745.name: Vector Length
8204e027-2b1d-5a71-8ec5-11a868ae6745.behavior: One of two equivalent ways to get a curvature value (the other: 1/osculating-circle-radius via Deconstruct Arc + Division).

6ec39468-dae7-4ffa-a766-f2ab22a2c62e.name: Amplitude
6ec39468-dae7-4ffa-a766-f2ab22a2c62e.behavior: Rescales a vector to a target length while preserving direction/sense. In the surface-conforming Weaving tutorial, driven by the LOCAL surface normal (from Divide Surface) rather than a fixed world direction, so a woven pattern can conform to any surface — explicit warning: "make sure the data structure of normals and points match."

5f4e4711-d6d3-5175-8776-68845c80a89a.name: Distance
5f4e4711-d6d3-5175-8776-68845c80a89a.behavior: Computes the distance between two points; used to measure attractor-to-geometry distance, and (with a target value) as the Fitness basis for goal-seeking optimization.

3581f42a-9592-4549-bd6b-1c0fc39d067b.name: Construct Point
3581f42a-9592-4549-bd6b-1c0fc39d067b.behavior: Computes a point from x/y/z; distinct from the container "Point" component despite sharing the "Pt" abbreviation on canvas. Default input data 0,0,0 places a point at the world origin.

5650d832-9c6d-5a3a-a644-cdceb28dc5c6.name: Deconstruct (point) / Point Decompose
5650d832-9c6d-5a3a-a644-cdceb28dc5c6.behavior: Used as a sort-key source (feed X or Y output into Sort List's K) to recover grid order from geometry when list order is scrambled.

4716a53e-f34e-5795-8f35-498d5b556179.name: DePlane
4716a53e-f34e-5795-8f35-498d5b556179.behavior: Deconstructs a plane into origin + 3 axis vectors; used as an intermediate step to extract a circle's plane/origin so Scale can use it as the scale center.

outputs.name: Pl
outputs.description: a new plane with B's orientation relocated to origin O

d3770ee4-7f6e-5dd4-83a4-17c98bf3c3d8.name: Plane Normal
d3770ee4-7f6e-5dd4-83a4-17c98bf3c3d8.behavior: Builds a plane from an origin + a normal vector (e.g. a surface normal from Evaluate Surface), used to derive a rotation plane from geometry, or a panel's local offset direction for non-coplanar panel arrays.

0fd73e79-7739-5207-8bd8-876aad6d298a.name: Construct Plane

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: "X-Axis", Vector — X-axis direction of the plane

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: "Y-Axis", Vector — Y-axis direction of the plane

0fd73e79-7739-5207-8bd8-876aad6d298a.behavior: CORRECTED — a real, distinct component from Plane Normal (above), not a probable duplicate. If AAD p.269's partly-illegible diagram genuinely showed only two inputs (O and one vector), that diagram was more likely depicting Plane Normal (or another 2-input plane constructor) rather than this 3-input component.

5d5485bc-3059-5498-9c46-500902ef2fc6.name: Square Grid

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: Points, tree — one branch per row/column

5d5485bc-3059-5498-9c46-500902ef2fc6.behavior: Ex controls the number of tree branches in the output point tree; Ey controls the number of items per branch.

d044f643-7637-599c-bf14-5c4beb10e8d7.name: Reverse (vector)

outputs.name: V
outputs.description: "Vector", Vector — reversed vector, i.e. multiplied by -1

d044f643-7637-599c-bf14-5c4beb10e8d7.behavior: Used to invert a face-normal direction when it does not match the required sense relative to another vector (e.g. a solar-ray vector) — direction requirement is context-dependent (e.g. must point inward for one recipe, outward for another); always verify with Vector Display first. CORRECTED/MERGED: this is the same real component as the KB's separate "Negate (vector)" entry (AAD p.376, gravity-vector usage feeding Catenary's G input) — both describe a Vector > Vector sign-flip with identical V→V ports. No standalone "Negate" component exists in GH1; the two AAD citations (p.376 and p.451/454) are merged into this one entry.
d044f643-7637-599c-bf14-5c4beb10e8d7.provenance: [STATED, AAD p.451, 454] [STATED, AAD p.376 as "Negate"/alias "Neg" — merged, same component] [VERIFIED https://grasshopperdocs.com/components/grasshoppervector/reverse.html]

807b86e3-be8d-4970-92b5-f8cdcb45b06b.name: Circle (plane + radius)
807b86e3-be8d-4970-92b5-f8cdcb45b06b.behavior: Constructs a circle from a plane and radius — the first Grasshopper component shown in AAD, wired to a Radius slider.

d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.name: Circle CNR (center + normal + radius)
d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.behavior: Builds the circle's plane implicitly from a point+normal instead of a full Plane — convenient when normals come from curve/surface evaluation (e.g. Eval.T or Evaluate Surface.N). AAD explicitly names "Circle CNR"; Essential shows the identical port shape (center, normal, radius) simply labeled "Circle" — treated as the same component.
d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.provenance: [STATED, AAD p.112 (used unnamed as "Circle"), 178 (formally named), 204; Essential p.32, 46]

4183b8ca-95f3-5df5-9480-6fec2b8a1d92.name: Arc 3Pt

inputs.name: B
inputs.description: "Point B", Point — point the arc passes through

outputs.name: P
outputs.description: "Plane", Plane — the plane containing the arc

4183b8ca-95f3-5df5-9480-6fec2b8a1d92.behavior: Creates an arc through three points; A and C are endpoints, B is a point the arc passes through. Used to build a pre-set arc-length (e.g. forcing a 10-unit-span arc to have arc-length exactly 20) as the starting geometry for a near-inextensible catenary approximation.

4c4e56eb-2f04-43f9-95a3-cc46a14f495a.name: Line (2-point)
4c4e56eb-2f04-43f9-95a3-cc46a14f495a.behavior: Builds a line from two points; shows orange/warning if A/B unconnected, red/error if a wrong type is wired (e.g. a raw Number into a Point input — "Data conversion failed from Number to Point"). With two point lists (e.g. from dividing concentric circles), connects corresponding points; combining with Shift List on one list changes which points pair up, producing different radial/spoke patterns.

4c619bc9-39fd-4717-82a6-1e07ea237bbe.name: Line SDL
4c619bc9-39fd-4717-82a6-1e07ea237bbe.behavior: Builds a line from a start point + direction + length — distinct from the two-point Line component (A/B inputs); used e.g. to offset an "apex" point above a sub-surface center along its normal.

62e19838-56a1-504f-90f1-a347350970a9.name: Point on Curve

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: implicit) + value 0-1 (rendered as a slider-bar on the component's face

62e19838-56a1-504f-90f1-a347350970a9.behavior: Finds a point via fractional ARC LENGTH (not domain parameter t) — 0.5 is always the true geometric midpoint; does not require reparameterization. Right-click named snaps: 0.0(start)/1/4(quarter)/1/3(third)/1/2(mid)/2/3(two thirds)/3/4(three quarters)/1.0(end). CONTRASTS with Evaluate Curve (domain-parameter-based, not arc-length-based) — a Grasshopper-native substitute for CAD Osnap "midpoint" picking.

11bbd48b-bb0a-4f1b-8167-fa297590390d.name: End Points
11bbd48b-bb0a-4f1b-8167-fa297590390d.tab: Curve > Analysis (RESOLVED — AAD p.160's "Endpoint"/Curve > Util reference is an internal inconsistency, likely mislabeling of an in-context screenshot; "End Points"/Curve > Analysis is correct)
11bbd48b-bb0a-4f1b-8167-fa297590390d.behavior: Extracts a curve's two endpoints — a Grasshopper-native substitute for CAD Osnap "endpoint" picking.
11bbd48b-bb0a-4f1b-8167-fa297590390d.provenance: [STATED, AAD p.62, 160, 303, 366; Essential p.19 general list mention] [VERIFIED https://grasshopperdocs.com/components/grasshoppercurve/endPoints.html]

fc6979e4-7e91-4508-8e05-37c680779751.name: Evaluate Curve [DISAMBIGUATION 2 of 3 — see Evaluate F(X) under Maths, Evaluate Length below]

outputs.name: A
outputs.description: "Angle", Number — angle in radians between the incoming vs. outgoing curve direction at t; a discontinuity measure, not curvature

fc6979e4-7e91-4508-8e05-37c680779751.behavior: Finds point + tangent vector at DOMAIN parameter t — NOT arc-length (t=0.5 is generally NOT the true midpoint unless the curve is reparameterized AND happens to be uniform). Renders as a plain "Eval" box identical to Evaluate F(X) and Evaluate Length; distinguish by its C/t ports and Curve > Analysis tab. Combined with Random + Sort: Random generates unordered curve parameters, which MUST be Sorted (ascending) before feeding to Eval, else resulting points/circles are visited out of curve order, producing a twisted/self-intersecting Loft.

6b021f56-b194-4210-b9a1-6cef3b7d0848.name: Evaluate Length [DISAMBIGUATION 3 of 3 — see Evaluate F(X) under Maths, Evaluate Curve above]

inputs.name: N
inputs.description: "Normalized", Boolean — if True, L is read as a normalized 0.0-1.0 fraction of total curve length; if False, L is read as an absolute length in curve/model units; AAD's example implicitly uses N=False/absolute-length mode

6b021f56-b194-4210-b9a1-6cef3b7d0848.behavior: Finds the point located a given arc-length distance L from the curve's start (t=0). Renders as a plain "Eval" box identical to Evaluate F(X) and Evaluate Curve; distinguish by its C/L/N ports and Curve > Analysis tab.

2162e72e-72fc-4bf8-9459-d4d82fa8aa14.name: Divide Curve

inputs.name: K
inputs.description: "Kinks", Boolean — when True, adds extra split points at the curve's discontinuities/direction changes

outputs.name: T
outputs.description: "Tangents", Vector — tangent direction at each point

outputs.name: t
outputs.description: "Parameters", Number — the curve parameter at each point

2162e72e-72fc-4bf8-9459-d4d82fa8aa14.behavior: Divides an open or closed curve into equal arc-length segments: N+1 points for an open curve, exactly N points for a closed curve (e.g. dividing a circle into 5 gives 5 points, since start/end coincide). Output points ordered by the curve's parametric start-to-end direction. Dividing a SINGLE curve gives a flat list; dividing a LIST of curves gives a tree (one branch per curve) — a key example of components that add tree nesting.

a17bd1ea-0b43-5207-968b-66d301f6b294.name: Divide Length
a17bd1ea-0b43-5207-968b-66d301f6b294.behavior: Divides a curve into fixed absolute-length segments; leaves a "leftover-arc" of different length at the end if the curve's total length isn't an exact multiple of L.

7e0f577e-8a4d-5e4c-a8b7-a562170de88b.name: Divide Distance
7e0f577e-8a4d-5e4c-a8b7-a562170de88b.behavior: Divides a curve via sequential intersections of circles of radius D (centered at each successively-found point) with the curve — geometrically distinct from Divide Length. Leaves a leftover-arc if D doesn't evenly divide the curve. A single boundary edge can supply both plane-origin points (via Divide Distance) and a constant slicing direction (via Vector 2Pt) for parallel cutting planes.

3748786b-8a93-5377-bb38-bbd391539dfb.name: Contour

inputs.name: D
inputs.description: Distance, Number — spacing between cutting planes

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: "Contours", Point — intersection points, grouped by section

outputs.name: t
outputs.description: "Parameters", Number — curve parameter of each contour point

3748786b-8a93-5377-bb38-bbd391539dfb.behavior: Intersects a curve with a family of parallel cutting lines/planes spaced D apart along direction N, starting from point P.

6d332a03-1ccb-57d5-870b-51a6192a010d.name: Shatter

inputs.name: t
inputs.description: list of split parameters, LCS [0,1] domain

6d332a03-1ccb-57d5-870b-51a6192a010d.behavior: Splits a curve into segments AT given t-parameters — returns curve pieces, not points (unlike other Division-family components). The t-input can be a slider, Curve CP's t-output, or Divide Curve's t-output. RESOLVED: this is a real, distinct component from Explode Curve (Curve > Util, below). AAD p.378's diagram labeled "Explode" with ports C,R → S,V is NOT a mislabeled Shatter — its ports exactly match the real, separate Explode component's spec (Shatter has no R input and no V output), so it is the book's own surrounding text (still calling it "Shatter" in context on that page) that is wrong, not the diagram label.

088423c5-f95a-5023-98f9-aa1e8c4e1afc.name: Curvature
088423c5-f95a-5023-98f9-aa1e8c4e1afc.behavior: Returns the curvature vector and osculating circle (best-fit circle) at a point on a curve; k = |K| = 1/r (osculating circle radius).

4b406827-4654-5488-b637-e58105a0c848.name: Curvature Graph
4b406827-4654-5488-b637-e58105a0c848.behavior: Visually displays curvature along a curve as a comb of perpendicular hairlines, length proportional to curvature magnitude, +/- signs marking curvature-sign regions.

4a7b72d7-7a17-5985-a7fe-33bdc5e7f895.name: Flip Curve [shares nickname "Flip" with the unrelated Flip Matrix (Sets > Tree) — see that entry's disambiguation note]
4a7b72d7-7a17-5985-a7fe-33bdc5e7f895.behavior: Reverses a curve's parametric direction (swaps t=0/t=1 ends). With G supplied plus a list of mixed-direction curves at C, flips only curves not already matching G's direction, in one operation. Does NOT fix curve direction via Reparameterize — these are independent operations (direction is set by original control-point order).

0e9e34bd-4b08-53ae-b34d-95adaefb8c00.name: Curve Closest Point
0e9e34bd-4b08-53ae-b34d-95adaefb8c00.behavior: World-to-Local conversion for curves — finds closest point on curve to a given point, returns the distance; if P lies exactly on the curve, P=P' and D=0. Implements curve-based attractors.

295cfb7a-b5b4-5457-a3fa-536f471cfcc0.name: Deconstruct Arc
295cfb7a-b5b4-5457-a3fa-536f471cfcc0.behavior: Breaks an arc (incl. a circle, a closed arc) into base plane, radius, and angle domain.

2b2a4145-3dff-41d4-a8de-1ea9d29eef33.name: Interpolate Curve (official GH1 name: "Interpolate")
2b2a4145-3dff-41d4-a8de-1ea9d29eef33.behavior: Draws a curve interpolated through a list of points. Used repeatedly to fit a smooth curve through Kangaroo particle positions for visual continuity — a caveat applies: this can look smooth but is physically incorrect at multi-anchor junctions since it implies bending stiffness a hinge-particle simulation cannot have. CORRECTED (naming): the current GH1 component's official name is "Interpolate" (nickname "IntCrv"), not "Interpolate Curve" — a naming nuance, not a factual error in the port data. COMPLETED: the extra L/D outputs are real (Length, Domain), not an over-guess — the source's own hedge undersold what AAD/Essential correctly showed as 3 outputs.

42a28fc5-40a8-540b-ab70-5a754d22af8a.name: Nurbs Curve
42a28fc5-40a8-540b-ab70-5a754d22af8a.behavior: Rebuilds a smooth freeform curve through a point list — used to fix sharp-corner discontinuities introduced by a raw Offset, and to rebuild a smooth silhouette from a twisted-loft isocurve extraction. Confirmed to share the same L/D output pattern as Interpolate Curve, exactly as previously guessed by analogy.

71b5b089-500a-4ea6-81c5-2f960441a0e8.name: Polyline
71b5b089-500a-4ea6-81c5-2f960441a0e8.behavior: Operates PER BRANCH on tree-structured input — a component fed N branches produces N separate polylines, not one continuous one (core illustration of "branches are watertight").

e41c19b3-ca2b-5901-8959-74ae1563ade8.name: Isocurve
e41c19b3-ca2b-5901-8959-74ae1563ade8.behavior: Extracts the two isocurves passing through a given uv point.

40c17387-b778-5913-b397-6db79db3accf.name: Curve on Surface

inputs.name: uv
inputs.description: "UV coordinates", Point — list/tree of uv interpolation points, from Merge

inputs.name: C
inputs.description: "Closed", Boolean — whether the resulting curve is closed

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: "Curve", Curve — resulting NURBS curve coincident to the surface

40c17387-b778-5913-b397-6db79db3accf.behavior: Creates an interpolated curve on a surface through an arbitrary set of uv points in the surface's Local Coordinate System — used to build a Galapagos-optimized shortest path across a freeform surface. Note the component reuses nickname "C" for both an input (Closed) and an output (Curve).

0424ac40-4f1a-5441-9332-9e8d221fcb0c.name: Offset (curve)
0424ac40-4f1a-5441-9332-9e8d221fcb0c.behavior: Generic planar/3D curve offset (not surface-constrained — contrast Offset on Srf below). Offsetting a curve with sharp corners can introduce discontinuities/kinks at those corners — fix: divide the offset into many points and rebuild via Nurbs Curve.

04414706-dc4e-56e9-bfa3-406bcff522fc.name: Offset on Srf

inputs.name: S
inputs.description: surface(s) to keep the offset coincident to

04414706-dc4e-56e9-bfa3-406bcff522fc.behavior: Unlike a generic curve offset, keeps the result coincident with a host surface — required so an inward-offset "frame" curve of a curved panel stays flush with the panel sub-surface rather than drifting off it in 3D.

ebcd61dd-adda-52c5-9f6a-994483a9986d.name: Explode Curve [3-WAY NAME CONFLICT: "Explode" is shared by this component (Curve > Util), by a Mesh > Util component that explodes a mesh into faces, and by a Mesh > Analysis "Mesh Explode" — disambiguate by tab and by whether the input is a curve or a mesh]
ebcd61dd-adda-52c5-9f6a-994483a9986d.behavior: Breaks a polyline/polycurve into its constituent segments and vertices.

1fc87e4b-8bd9-5462-a444-a5ca3c629e49.name: Discontinuity
1fc87e4b-8bd9-5462-a444-a5ca3c629e49.behavior: Returns one branch of points per input curve (e.g. turns each Voronoi cell — a single closed curve — into its own branch of boundary vertex points).

2e888ac3-63d9-590f-83ab-ea618c5af23c.name: Project
2e888ac3-63d9-590f-83ab-ea618c5af23c.behavior: Projects a curve onto a target surface, replacing straight segments with true surface-coincident curves — essential post-step for diagrid construction (a diagrid floats off a curved surface except at corners; Project snaps it back).

eab009af-01c9-5b20-98c9-83c5ae7beb0c.name: Extrude
eab009af-01c9-5b20-98c9-83c5ae7beb0c.behavior: Extrudes a base curve/brep along a direction vector — "the easiest way to create a surface."

a7a41d0a-2188-4f7a-82cc-1a2c4e4ec850.name: Loft
a7a41d0a-2188-4f7a-82cc-1a2c4e4ec850.behavior: Generates a surface through a set of section curves.

73a63cba-b1bb-5980-8662-f24891f1da6e.name: Loft Options
73a63cba-b1bb-5980-8662-f24891f1da6e.behavior: Sets loft behavior; rebuild needed when too few section curves exist for a smooth surface.

d51e9b65-aa4e-4fd6-976c-cef35d421d05.name: Boundary Surfaces
d51e9b65-aa4e-4fd6-976c-cef35d421d05.behavior: Creates a flat planar surface bounded by closed curve(s); also usable as an implicit planarity test (only produces a surface if the boundary curves are planar).

59fa27d2-a01d-556b-9bb4-98cb860d7035.name: Surface from Points

inputs.name: P
inputs.description: Points — grid of points, must be pre-ordered row-by-row/column-by-column and set to flatten mode

inputs.name: U
inputs.description: U Count — number of points in u-direction, integer

inputs.name: I

59fa27d2-a01d-556b-9bb4-98cb860d7035.behavior: Builds a surface from a rectangular grid of points; needs an explicit U count to know how many points lie in one direction (obtained e.g. via List Length on a Range output). WARNING: assumes the input list is already sequenced in row/column grid order — a geometrically-correct but list-order-scrambled point set produces a severely malformed, self-intersecting surface with NO error raised.

c6fc271c-c2a7-5680-98d4-7e6c50b4e214.name: Edge Surface
c6fc271c-c2a7-5680-98d4-7e6c50b4e214.behavior: Creates a surface interpolating between 2-4 ordered boundary/edge curves. Can only cap boundaries of exactly 4 edges — N-sided openings (e.g. hexagons) require a different capping strategy (two Lofts between opposite edge pairs, or Patch as a general alternative).

57b2184c-8931-4e70-9220-612ec5b3809a.name: Patch
57b2184c-8931-4e70-9220-612ec5b3809a.behavior: Fits a surface using perpendicular "span" curves generated from the input; spans rarely align with the output surface's edges — a fallback when other surfacing methods aren't feasible (e.g. general-purpose N-sided capping).

1a8d5f23-3b25-56b1-b7b5-d616f22f544f.name: Network Surface

outputs.name: S
outputs.description: surface fit through the two curve families

1a8d5f23-3b25-56b1-b7b5-d616f22f544f.behavior: Builds one surface from two ordered curve sets — more edge control than Loft. Also usable as an alternative weave finish: if warp/weft threads are allowed to touch (skip the Negative-vector step), the resulting curve network can be fed directly into Network Surface for one continuous quilted surface instead of discrete piped tubes.

b5d8c4a4-e69b-5f56-8063-3ee3e6520d29.name: Revolution
b5d8c4a4-e69b-5f56-8063-3ee3e6520d29.behavior: Revolves a profile curve around a fixed axis.

96f8ed6b-9933-5994-b26c-63f7bbc7c5a4.name: Rail Revolution

inputs.name: A
inputs.description: revolution axis line, per one usage

96f8ed6b-9933-5994-b26c-63f7bbc7c5a4.behavior: Revolves a profile using a rail curve instead of a fixed axis, letting the axis itself vary along the rail — used to rebuild a smooth-edged surface of revolution replacing a sharp-edged twisted Loft.

c277f778-6fdf-4890-8f78-347efb23c406.name: Pipe
c277f778-6fdf-4890-8f78-347efb23c406.behavior: Sweeps a circular cross-section of given radius along one or more rail curves — e.g. turns a wireframe diagrid into a tubular 3D structure, or a woven thread curve into a solid member.

e1ea342b-8ace-5af3-93f1-a19001303d6c.name: Surface CP
e1ea342b-8ace-5af3-93f1-a19001303d6c.behavior: World-to-Local conversion for surfaces (surface analog of Curve CP); if the input point lies on the surface, P=P' and D=0.

5106bafc-d5d4-4983-83e7-7be3ed07f502.name: Divide Surface
5106bafc-d5d4-4983-83e7-7be3ed07f502.behavior: Generates a grid of points at isocurve intersections dividing u/v evenly by the given integer counts. Dividing a single surface produces a TREE of points (a grid), one branch per row/column. Its natural U+1-branches x V-items output tree is exploited directly as the "warp" direction of a weave, and Flip-Matrix-transposed to get the "weft" direction for free.

39619e60-8f3e-53bd-b984-c6bd01fe1c19.name: Isotrim
39619e60-8f3e-53bd-b984-c6bd01fe1c19.behavior: Splits a surface into contiguous untrimmed sub-surfaces per a supplied grid of sub-domains (typically from Divide Domain²). Output sub-surfaces KEEP the original parent surface's domain (not reset to [0,1]) unless explicitly Reparameterized.

054e6f88-634c-5777-9da1-375908a63e56.name: Deconstruct Brep
054e6f88-634c-5777-9da1-375908a63e56.behavior: Extracts all constituent faces, edges, vertices of any Brep. When fed a list of N sub-surfaces at once, each downstream List Item(i=k) extracts "vertex slot k of every sub-surface" as one flat parallel list (implicit grouping, not explicit tree manipulation) — key to scaling single-item recipes (e.g. a diagrid) to whole-surface recipes.

45358253-0a77-5342-8d4b-6bd3e0f809cb.name: Center Box
45358253-0a77-5342-8d4b-6bd3e0f809cb.behavior: Builds a box primitive; output is a Brep not a single Surface — wiring directly into a Surface-typed parameter causes a red type-mismatch error; fix: Deconstruct Brep first.

c4872015-a8eb-5504-9797-af873493ab27.name: Bounding Box

c4872015-a8eb-5504-9797-af873493ab27.behavior: Right-click mode toggle: "Per Object" (one bbox per input geometry) vs. "Union Box" (one box enclosing all input geometries together).

dfdec590-f5ae-57b0-9cbd-01d6e92403e4.name: Geodesic
dfdec590-f5ae-57b0-9cbd-01d6e92403e4.behavior: Constructs the shortest-path curve ("straight line in curved space") between two points on a surface — used as a natural cutting curve for Surface Split, and (per a guest project) as the basis of a gridshell panelization pattern.

inputs.name: uv
inputs.description: point in UV domain, e.g. MD Slider

425f42c2-d6c7-59ca-a429-f37667072c5d.behavior: At point P on a surface, C1 = curve of minimum curvature K1, C2 = curve of maximum curvature K2 through P; directions always perpendicular.

8d5b46de-2499-5af1-b826-6561af8c6151.name: Surface Curvature [NAME CONFLICT: nicknamed "Curvature" — see Principal Curvature above]
8d5b46de-2499-5af1-b826-6561af8c6151.behavior: G = K1·K2 (product of principal curvatures; G=0 developable, G>0 synclastic/dome, G<0 anticlastic/saddle); M = (K1+K2)/2 (M=0 defines minimal surfaces, e.g. catenoids/soap films). Signed-curvature convention: circles are defined as negative curvature, so e.g. a cylinder's M comes out negative — must Absolute-value before using as a physical quantity like radius.

5d3e74ab-368d-572d-a6a7-c3cf681c5968.behavior: Builds one triangular mesh face by topology (index references into a separate vertex list, not raw points); winding order (CCW) determines front/back orientation. 50616ef6-9fd9-5c8a-a195-dd02e4eac194.name: Construct Mesh
50616ef6-9fd9-5c8a-a195-dd02e4eac194.behavior: Assembles a mesh from a vertex list + face-index list (+ optional colors).

4bbb282f-86b4-5348-b018-fff1357214d6.name: Delaunay Mesh
4bbb282f-86b4-5348-b018-fff1357214d6.behavior: Triangulates an arbitrary point set maximizing minimum angle (avoids skinny/thin triangles that produce inaccurate FEM/particle-spring simulation results); formal rule: for each triangulated face, its circumscribed "Delaunay circle" must not contain any other point of the set. Operates per-branch on grafted/tree-structured input (one discrete disconnected mesh per branch — requires join+weld afterward to fuse).

16e4f9f7-debf-5cf4-a474-7b37a3a9d74a.behavior: NURBS-to-mesh conversion — reliable only for UNTRIMMED surfaces (clean rectangular isogrid maps directly to quad grid); trimmed surfaces only approximate their boundary via this component (Mesh Brep preserves exact boundary but risks skinny triangles near it). e7d65237-a208-5273-92ed-2607af15a367.name: Mesh Flip
e7d65237-a208-5273-92ed-2607af15a367.behavior: Fixes face-orientation incompatibility between adjoining meshes converted from different surfaces (visible as a shading/shadow artifact along the shared edge) before joining/welding/subdividing.

8e5a628b-136a-5062-bf18-df89ecdfcfdb.name: Voronoi
8e5a628b-136a-5062-bf18-df89ecdfcfdb.behavior: Decomposes space into cells, one per seed point, such that every location in a cell is closer to its seed than any other. No R input → defaults to infinite radius (full tessellation, cells share edges). Finite R → clips each cell to a circle of that radius (may overlap/leave gaps, not a clean tiling).

Feeding T with a LIST of vectors (e.g. an increasing Series through Unit Z) produces one translated copy per vector via default list matching — the book's standard technique for stacking/arraying copies of a single base object "for free."

4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.name: Scale
4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.tab: Transform > Affine (RESOLVED — AAD p.113-114/451-452's "Transform > Euclidean" citation is an internal inconsistency within the same book; p.196/323, Affine, is correct)
4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.behavior: Scales geometry by factor F about center point C (any point, not necessarily the object's own centroid). F must be a positive number and can never be exactly 0 ("a null scale factor is a mathematical error"); 0<F<1 shrinks, F=1 unchanged, F>1 enlarges. Supplying a LIST of factors (one per object, matched against a list of geometries and a list of per-object centers) lets each object scale independently.

b7798b74-037e-4f0c-8ac7-dc1043d093e0.name: Rotate

94d3d2d9-57bc-57ac-b690-49766522c2b5.name: Goat (exact/local optimization, by Simon Flöry)

inputs.name: Objective
inputs.description: exactly one numeric value to minimize/maximize

94d3d2d9-57bc-57ac-b690-49766522c2b5.behavior: Double-click opens "goat - Optimization Settings" dialog: "Optimize for" (Minimum/Maximum), "Optimization algorithm" dropdown (e.g. "Local, linear approximations (COBYLA)"), "Stop optimization if" checkboxes (relative change in objective/variables below threshold, objective below value, running time exceeds limit). Exact solver: always finds the single best solution, same result every run — contrast Galapagos (heuristic, varies run to run). Local algorithms can get stuck at local optima; for complex problems run Global first then refine Local. Used in AAD's worked examples to minimize point-to-curve distance and (in a guest essay) to minimize axial force in a graphical-statics funicular form.

inputs.name: D

inputs.name: B
inputs.description: Termination Condition — boolean or number; stops the loop when false, or when the iteration count is reached

inputs.name: T

outputs.name: C
outputs.description: Cumulative Feedback / Feedback History — one branch per iteration; grasshopperdocs calls it "C", the plugin's own source comments call it "H" — same output functionally

9cfb66da-31a8-5ad3-ab69-2ba031ab8d86.behavior: Emulates a loop despite GH's left-to-right-only solver logic (a true feedback wire is otherwise forbidden and would need to route a downstream output back into an upstream input). Edge-condition geometry → S-input, passes through unchanged as F; loop body's final output → D-input closes the loop; B sets iteration count. Does NOT run within GH's normal automatic solver — must be manually started via its own floating control panel (double-click to open): Step (one iteration), Auto Loop All (runs until iteration counter I = B), Reset All. Used to generate a 3D Koch-snowflake fractal (recursive triangle subdivision) and a spiral "galaxy-like" roof mesh (recursive vector move+rotate, driven by a live Ecotect sun-angle imported via Geco).

8ac6bfc6-74bb-5d15-92d3-3788bd2a5331.behavior: Iterates a procedure by substituting an output parameter of the procedure's FINAL component into an input parameter of the procedure's INITIAL component — closes a loop "by reference" rather than a direct feedback wire; typically paired with a Timer for continuous refresh. 21607441-507e-59e8-bd6e-8fc855d6d4e9.name: Galapagos (Genome / Fitness)
21607441-507e-59e8-bd6e-8fc855d6d4e9.tab: Params > Util (native Grasshopper genetic solver, by David Rutten)
21607441-507e-59e8-bd6e-8fc855d6d4e9.behavior: Double-click opens the "Galapagos Editor" (tabs Options/Solvers/Record): Options — Fitness Minimize/Maximize dropdown, Threshold, Runtime Limit; Evolutionary Solver settings (Max Stagnant, Population, Initial Boost); Solvers tab — Start/Stop Solver, live fitness-range graph, ranked candidate list. Heuristic solver: a population of candidates evolves via mutation/crossover/selection; NO run-to-run guarantee of an identical result (unlike the exact solver Goat). Best suited for large variable counts where no exact solver applies. Cannot be driven by a Graph Mapper (its internal curve is not slider-drivable, so it cannot itself be a Genome input — expose the sliders that feed it instead). Runs indefinitely; must be manually stopped once the top candidate's fitness stabilizes. Worked example: cantilever cross-section shape optimization (Karamba) — topology fixed, only CroSecSelect's index varies — reduced tip displacement from 0.009703 (index 29) to 0.000253 (index 89 optimum), ~38x improvement. Also used to find the shortest interpolated path between two fixed points on a freeform surface via Gene Pool-driven uv control points, and (per a guest essay) to re-solve a fabrication-constrained panelization for a smaller laser-cutter bed without redesigning the geometry.

a784fcb0-a174-5343-a2af-4c2b343d6df3.name: Gene Pool
a784fcb0-a174-5343-a2af-4c2b343d6df3.tab: Params > Util (native GH component supporting Galapagos)
a784fcb0-a174-5343-a2af-4c2b343d6df3.behavior: Embeds a configurable collection of Number Sliders in one component; double-click sets Gene Count, slider range (min/max), significant digits. More sliders = higher accuracy of the resulting optimized curve/geometry.
